run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-14T22:43:12Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert's nonzero error rate on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is real and reproducible in telemetry: frontend-proxy's only non-UNSET span status over 21:43:12-23:04:37 is STATUS_CODE_ERROR (143.2 ingress, 94.5 egress error spans), and its own access log records those responses as 503 with flags 'UC' and reason 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' against the upstream cluster 'frontend'. Trace evidence shows the failed requests being forwarded to frontend and the connection cut with http.status_code "0", with no frontend span in the sampled trace. The error rate is not steady: a background of ~1-4 error spans per 2 minutes, a burst at 22:25-22:26, and the largest burst at ~22:46-22:48. The largest burst aligns with a cart Deployment rollout that replaced cart's only pod at 22:45:42-22:45:45 (new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d, old cart-755465879b scaled to 0), and in exactly the two overlapping 120s windows covering that replacement the frontend emitted its only gRPC error spans (CartService/AddItem 69.3, GetCart 30.7, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 24) and its only server error spans (GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout), while cart and checkout themselves show zero error spans. A contributing condition, not a proven trigger, is that the frontend container runs with a 100m CPU limit at ~0.054 cores and is throttled in 33-37% of CFS periods throughout 22:28-22:58. The final in-process reason the frontend terminates connections is not observable: frontend application logs returned no lines, Jaeger has no data after ~22:31:38, and the alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not loaded in this Prometheus.

claims.text: frontend-proxy exposes exactly two operations, 'ingress' (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client); over 21:43:12-23:04:37 the only non-UNSET status it recorded was STATUS_CODE_ERROR: increase 143.2 error spans on 'ingress' and 94.5 on 'router frontend egress' (UNSET: 22299.9 and 22352.9).

frontend-proxy's access log records the failures as 503 with response flag 'UC' and the exact error 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for upstream 'frontend', e.g. 2026-11-14T22:43:59.245Z 'GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP' and 2026-11-14T22:46:59.717Z-22:48:05.557Z for /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z, LS4PSXUNUM, 9SIQT8TOJO, 2ZYFJ3GM2N.

In trace c40b3222b9a63859e138ddf42bd9991a the chain observed is load-generator 'GET' (error=true, http.status_code 503) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' (error=true, http.status_code 503) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (error="true", http.status_code "0"), duration 892910us; that trace contains no span of service 'frontend'. A 5-trace sample of error=true frontend-proxy traces (22:26:42-22:31:03) shows the same pattern: 5 ingress spans error=true/http 503 with 5 egress spans error="true"/http.status_code "0".

frontend-proxy ingress error spans are intermittent rather than continuous: increase over 120s is 1.3-4 spans at most sampled minutes, 51.7 at 22:25:12Z and 37.3 at 22:26:12Z, 124 at 22:47:12Z and 128 at 22:48:12Z, and 0 at 22:38:12Z-22:43:12Z.

The frontend service itself recorded 421 error spans in the 5-minute window ending 22:48:12Z and 0 in the other sampled 5-minute windows; in that burst they are GET 25.6 and POST 77.8 server spans plus client spans grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 57.8, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 25.6, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 20, 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 83.3, '/api/checkout' 20 and tcp.connect 7.8.

At 60s resolution the frontend's gRPC error spans (CartService/AddItem 69.3, CartService/GetCart 30.7, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 24 per 120s) are nonzero only in the two overlapping 120s windows ending 22:47:12Z and 22:48:12Z, and are 0 at every other sample from 22:25:12Z to 22:58:12Z.

The cart Deployment replaced its only pod during that burst: ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d 'Scaled up ... from 0 to 1' and SuccessfulCreate of pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz at 22:45:42Z, 'Stopping container cart' on cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and ReplicaSet cart-755465879b 'Scaled down ... from 1 to 0' at 22:45:45Z; both ReplicaSets carry the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, so this is a configuration-only revision change.

The new cart container cart-84889c965d-tkxdz started at 22:45:44Z but its stdout begins only at 22:46:07.911Z with the startup line 'Overriding HTTP_PORTS ... Binding to values defined by URLS instead', and no error/failure line was found in its logs for the window; the previous cart pod (cart-755465879b-rh5r4) no longer exists and its logs are unavailable.

cart and checkout recorded 0 error spans in the 5-minute window ending 22:48:12Z; cart's server spans POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, /AddItem and /EmptyCart are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET and their per-10-minute counts continue at 1816/1897/1926 for GetCart across 22:23-22:53Z.

All otel-demo pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh (restartCount 1); all 21 Deployments were created 2026-11-14T22:14:32Z and report 1/1 ready, and the cart pod (22:45:42Z) is the only pod younger than that batch.

Service endpoints exist and point at live pods: frontend -> 100.96.3.35 (frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8), cart -> 100.96.1.157 (cart-84889c965d-tkxdz), checkout -> 100.96.3.7 (checkout-5dccddf8bb-cph2g), frontend-proxy -> 100.96.3.80; no ingress objects were returned for otel-demo.

The frontend container runs with limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi; its CPU burn is 0.040-0.057 cores per 5-minute sample (about 54% of the 100m limit at most samples), its CFS throttled-period ratio is 33.1-37.4% at every sample from 22:28:12Z to 22:58:12Z, and its maximum working set over the window is 130211840 bytes (130MB of 200Mi).

frontend-proxy's own resource signals are modest: container CFS throttled ratio 0.068-0.104, maximum working set 20594688 bytes of a 50Mi limit, and ingress p95 latency 678-802ms in the four samples before the burst, 921ms at 22:48:12Z, then 764ms and 761ms.

frontend's 'GET /api/cart' p95 latency was 190-238ms in the four samples 22:28:12Z-22:43:12Z and 369.6ms / 373.1ms / 341.8ms at 22:48:12Z / 22:53:12Z / 22:58:12Z, i.e. it rose coincident with the cart pod replacement and stayed higher within the observed samples.

Primary supported chain for the largest burst: frontend-proxy's 503s are produced by its upstream 'frontend' terminating the connection before a response starts; the frontend in turn failed its cart/checkout calls (its only gRPC client error spans) in exactly the windows covering the cart Deployment's pod replacement at 22:45:42-22:45:45, when cart's only replica was replaced and the new cart process only began logging at 22:46:07, i.e. a short cart-unavailability window. This alignment is strong but not proven as causation (span-export timing is only resolvable to ~1-2 minutes).

Second remaining candidate for the continuous background of 503s (present at 22:25-22:26, 22:29-22:41 and 22:53-22:58, i.e. outside the cart rollout): the frontend is CPU-starved at its 100m limit (about 0.054 cores used, 33-37% of CFS periods throttled for the whole observed period) and aborts/resets requests under load; this cannot be confirmed because those minutes have no frontend error spans and Jaeger holds no trace data after ~22:31:38.

The old cart pod may have been returning failing responses in its final seconds before termination; cart's spans carry no error status at all (always STATUS_CODE_UNSET), so its spans cannot prove success, and the old pod's logs are gone. This stays an open alternative to 'cart was simply unavailable during the swap'.

cart and checkout show no error evidence of their own in the burst window (0 error spans for both at 22:48:12Z) and the cart pod is Running, ready, restartCount 0 with a correctly populated endpoint, so neither service is shown to be damaged; the cart pod was replaced by its own Deployment controller (SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete plus ScalingReplicaSet), which is a rollout, not a failure.

The error rate is not explained by the cart replacement alone: frontend-proxy already had error bursts at 22:25:12Z/22:26:12Z (51.7/37.3 error spans per 120s) well before the cart rollout, and it kept emitting 1.3-5.3 error spans per 120s after 22:48:12Z, when the frontend's own error spans were back to 0.

Rejected as the primary cause: frontend-proxy being itself resource-exhausted or misrouted. Its CFS throttling is only 0.068-0.104, working set 20.6MB of 50Mi, ingress p95 latency stayed in the 678-921ms band, the 'frontend' Service has a live endpoint (100.96.3.35), and the error status sits on the egress span with http.status_code "0" and an access-log reason naming the upstream reset, so the failure is attributed to the upstream side of the proxy, not to the proxy's own capacity.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with label selector {alertname="RequestErrorRate"} both returned no_data, so the alert expression and the reported current value 0.01111111111111111 could not be verified.

Jaeger holds no trace data after ~2026-11-14T22:31:38Z (earliest returned trace data for the window was 22:26:42-22:31:03), so the 22:43-22:52 error burst has no span-level detail; the burst is only visible through span-derived metrics and pod access logs.

The frontend container's log stream returned no lines for the whole 21:43:12-23:04:37 window (no_data; previous instance unavailable), so no application-level error text exists from the service that terminates the connections.
The previous cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 was deleted, so its logs and behaviour in its final seconds are unknown.

frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration (route timeouts, circuit breakers, upstream settings) is not in any ConfigMap in otel-demo (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector, product-catalog-products were listed), so proxy-side settings could not be inspected; no ingress objects were returned for otel-demo either.

Access-log line count could not be used to quantify the error rate: the log lines' embedded timestamps (2025-12-15T17:4x) differ from their collection timestamps (2026-11-14T22:4x), and a 7-minute read of frontend-proxy logs contained only 7 lines matching ' 503 ' while span-derived error increases over the same minutes were far larger.
What configuration change created cart ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d at 22:45:42Z is unknown (image identical to the previous ReplicaSet); the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
Why frontend-proxy emitted its earlier burst at 22:25:12Z-22:26:12Z is unexplained: container metrics for these pods start at 22:28:12Z and the earliest available trace is 22:26:42Z.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh restarted its container at 22:51:13Z (Created/Started events, count 2) and now shows restartCount 1; the reason is unknown and no evidence ties it to frontend-proxy's 503s (it had 0 error spans in the sampled windows).

http_server_request_duration_seconds_count has no series in the queried window (no_data), so any HTTP-level error-rate reading for frontend-proxy is unknown rather than zero, and the alert's exact metric could not be reproduced.
The mechanism inside the frontend that resets the upstream connection (event-loop stall, request abort, connection limit, or application exception) is not observable from the retained evidence.
next_steps: Read the frontend container's application/stderr logs directly around 22:45-22:48Z (for example with the previous-instance flag) to capture the Node.js error that accompanies the connection termination.
Raise the frontend container's CPU limit above 100m (it burns ~0.054 cores and is throttled 33-37% of CFS periods) and re-check frontend-proxy's 503 rate afterwards.

Inspect the cart Deployment's revision history to learn what changed at 22:45:42Z (image unchanged) and why the only replica was replaced mid-traffic; consider a readiness gate or more than one replica so a cart rollout does not create a serving gap.

Retrieve the Alertmanager/Prometheus definition of RequestErrorRate (metric, window, threshold) from the monitoring stack, since this Prometheus instance does not carry that rule, to confirm which error-rate series the 0.0111 value came from.

Check whether frontend-proxy's Envoy route/upstream timeouts and circuit breakers are configured as intended (config is baked into image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy, not a ConfigMap).

Confirm the scope of the earlier 22:25-22:26Z burst with an independent metric source (for example node-level or load-generator telemetry), since neither traces nor container metrics cover those minutes here.
